description:
Team Wahdat will create a web tool with current locations on the Earth that analogue as optimal characteristics the environment on the Moon. 

A simulator will be also developed as part of the project for the equipment to be tested in advance if it will withstand the conditions on the Moon.
summary:
The main factors to identify locations on Earth similar to Moon are:
1. Extremely high and extremely low temperatures (Moon equator has temperatures ranging from 121 °C to -133 °C in the best case)
2. Strong winds (on the Moon - no atmosphere, strong solar winds hit it with a speed of 1 400 000 km/h in the best case).
3. Very small sand particles (regolith on the Moon is typically 10 times smaller than sand on Earth). 

The main obstacle on the Moon is abundance of sulfur in its inner core. Because of sulfur and other similar elements probably degraded a big part of the Moon’s inner core, Moon’s outer core became very similar to Earth’s mantle (oxygen and hydrogen are found in lunar crust, making it chemically possible to combine with sulfur into sulfuric acid H2SO4 catalysed by solar radiation and winds; thus, degrading metal ions found deeper, even at the level of the core and the mantle). 

So it is impossible to find such a place on Earth that mimic the Moon, so the best option is to test at first at the places from the tool on the address https://drive.google.com/file/d/16JEZeRyU1n4sRU7SqeeggEpMK7Y_tpdq/view 
All places from the tool are in the USA, for keeping safe US tech. 

And after to test on a simulator - that maximally mimic the Moon's conditions as temperatures, radioactivity, presence of fine sand, etc - the equipment finally, and the project for the simulator can be seen on the address https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1crTnog4eS-WsfH2AZ9uPtGFshfoitlrg/
details:
Many equipment units and machines currently fail or do not work as long and as expected once sent to the Moon. So the project offers an online tool with locations across the USA and a simulator that can be used to test equipment before it is sent to the Moon.

Criteria to use to identify locations on Earth similar to the Permanent Moon Base locations:
1. Extremely high and extremely low temperatures (Moon equator has temperatures ranging from 121 °C to -133 °C in the best case)
2. Strong winds (on the Moon - no atmosphere, strong solar winds hit it with a speed of 1 400 000 km/h in the best case).
3. Very small sand particles (regolith on the Moon is typically 10 times smaller than sand on Earth).

The conclusion is that it is impossible to find in Earth such a place that fully mimic the Moon's real environment and is even close enough to its characteristics – it doesn't exist. But a list of 10 locations with places identified that are a bit similar to the factors outlined above is offered in the tool on the address

https://drive.google.com/file/d/16JEZeRyU1n4sRU7SqeeggEpMK7Y_tpdq/view

Users can just download the index file from the drive link and open it as an index file, all locations shown as hyperlinks.

Locations are chosen as offering extremely hot or cold temperatures, strong winds and super fine sands. For maximal security and minimal ecological impact of the tests, locations are chosen far from human settlements, roads and water bodies.

The simulator from its part is described technically in the detailed project on the address

https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1crTnog4eS-WsfH2AZ9uPtGFshfoitlrg/

Users can just download the presentation and see the detailed description and its model.

The role of the simulator is to offer conditions that can't be found in nature as temperatures, air circulation, etc, so that equipment - once passing the tests on the locations from the tool - is finally tested inside the simulator in a harsher environment, giving it a better chance to withstand and work on the Permanent Moon Base locations.

Coding language used is HTML. Satellite data from Copernicus Europe and scientific data of NASA are used.
